page: Google Cloud Platform z3-highmem-192-highlssd-metal is a storage-optimized bare metal server powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, the machine delivers 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs at a base clock speed of 4.0 GHz, supported by 105 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 1,536 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. The server features an extensive local storage footprint of 77,304 GB across integrated NVMe SSDs, with no integrated GPU accelerators and no bundled complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded compute, memory bandwidth, and database performance. The instance achieved top-tier ratings in stress-ng multi-core CPU testing (160,589.01) and PassMark CPU benchmarks (122,607.65), heavily bolstered by instruction sets including AVX-512 and AMX. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 972.27 GB/sec, while PassMark database operations scored 35,531.62 and Redis SET throughput attained 183.57 million operations per second. Memory throughput remains robust at 462.85 GB/sec for large-block read operations. However, single-threaded execution is comparatively constrained, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring in the average tier and single-threaded gzip compression registering in the lower percentiles.

The bare metal configuration provides dedicated physical access, eliminating hypervisor overhead and virtualization jitter for disk-heavy and memory-intensive architectures. Cost efficiency is driven by the density of integrated NVMe storage paired with 1.5 TB of high-speed DDR5 RAM, allowing massive consolidation of distributed data platforms onto single physical nodes without relying on remote network storage. Given these hardware specifications, the server is engineered for extreme I/O workloads, large distributed transactional databases, massive in-memory caching systems, big data analytics engines, and high-concurrency real-time query serving.

Built on the x86_64 architecture, the server provides 1,536 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory (8 GB per vCPU) and a massive 77,304 GB array of local NVMe SSD storage, operating without a discrete GPU. In benchmark evaluations, the platform demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded compute, caching, and database throughput, logging 183.57 million Redis SET operations per second and strong multi-core PassMark ratings. Although single-core compression performance is average, the hardware eliminates virtualization overhead to offer dense capacity for high-throughput I/O architectures. This server is suited for high-scale database clusters, real-time analytics engines, in-memory key-value data stores, and extensive data processing pipelines requiring substantial local disk density.
